newsitem.title: USA: Limited to expand Victoria's Secret catalog.
newsitem.headline: Limited to expand Victoria's Secret catalog.

text.p: Limited Inc said Monday it plans to step up international expansion of its Victoria's Secret catalog operation during the next two to three years.
"It will be a virtually worldwide catalog," said Limited Chairman and Chief Executive Leslie Wexner during the retailer's annual meeting here.
Sales from the catalog were disappointing in 1996, rising just three percent from 1995 to $684 million, according to the company's annual report.

To boost sales, Victoria's Secret has begun to diversify. The company has launched specialty catalogs, including Swim, Country and City apparel books, and has big hopes for its push overseas, although it did not name other markets it plans to enter.
Europe is not currently on the expansion list, but it could be candidate in the future, said Cynthia Fedus, president of Victoria's Secret catalog during an interview.
"We really don't want to divert our attention (from Japan). We prefer to do a couple of things well and not a lot of things half way," she said.
Victoria's Secret is a division of Intimate Brands Inc, which Limited sold to the public in 1995. Limited retained an 83-percent stake in the company.
Intimate Brands Chief Financial Officer Philip Mallott said the company's growth model calls for earnings per share to increase by 16 percent and for sales to rise to $3.5 billion this year.
Last year Intimate Brands had net income of $258 million, or $1.02 a share. Sales increased to $3.0 billion from $2.5 billion in 1995.

Victoria's Secret catalog, which entered Japan last year, plans to open a telephone ordering center in Tokyo next month, Fedus said. It expects sales in the market to grow to at least $30 million in 1997 and to more than $150 million eventually. Sales in Japan last year were $15 million, up from $1.5 million in 1995.
In addition to overseas expansion, Victoria's Secret is experimenting with new lines of business. This autumn it will test a hosiery catalog.
Victoria's Secret retail division already operates 14 hosiery boutiques. Grace Nichols, president of Victoria's Secret store operation, said sales of hosiery could eventually reach $1 billion.
The company plans to add 65 Victoria's Secret stores this year, bringing the total to 801.

Intimate Brands Inc's toiletries division, Bath & Body Works, plans to open about 200 stores this year, bringing the total to 960. Bath & Body Works already has expanded to the UK and recently hired an executive to oversee international operations.
"We've received a number of inquiries for licensing and franchising Bath & Body Works on a global basis," Wexner said. "This is not imminent, but we're open to the idea."
